news.title: 'The time has come': Lionel Messi retires from international football
news.lede: Argentina superstar Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football, ending 21 years of national-team duty that were capped by winning the World Cup in 2022 to secure his place in the pantheon of the game's greatest ever players. “It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deeply — but I understand that the time has come,” the 39-year-old Messi said on his Instagram account. Messi, who will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, played in a record-tying six World Cups. He won it four years ago in a tournament he dominated in Qatar and also led Argentina to the title match in 2014 and again this year, when the Albiceleste lost to Spain in extra time in New Jersey.

news.title: Lionel Messi ends Argentina career after 21 years and World Cup glory
news.lede: Lionel Messi has retired from international football at 39, ending a 21-year Argentina career in which he overcame repeated disappointment to win the World Cup and become his country’s record scorer and most-capped player. Messi announced the decision on Monday, 31 August, six weeks after Argentina lost the 2026 World Cup final 1-0 to Spain in extra time. That match in New Jersey proved to be his final appearance for the national team. “It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep down, but I understand that the time has come,” Messi wrote on Instagram.

news.title: "Football is losing part of its soul": world newspapers react to the Messi bombshell
news.lede: Emotional reactions in the farewell to Argentina's legend. Lionel Messi announced his international retirement on Monday evening, and the world's sports newspapers cast it as the end of an exceptional chapter in the history of the Argentina national team and world football. Reaction to the surprise decision ranged from shock at its timing to a recalling of the numbers and titles, and to the void the former Argentina captain will leave after more than two decades in the shirt. Messi, "39 years old", broke the news in an emotional message.

news.title: Argentina’ Messi retires from international football
news.lede: KABUL (Pajhwok): Argentina captain Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football after leading his country to the 2022 World Cup title and the 2026 final. The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner is Argentina’s most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, with 207 appearances and 125 goals, Al Jazeera reported. “It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come,” the 39-year-old Messi wrote on Instagram on Monday. Messi said he had always given his best for the national team and believed the time had come for younger players to take his place.

news.title: SBS confirmed as Australia's home of the 2030 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: Football-loving Australians will have access to all 104 matches of the 2030 tournament via SBS television, video and radio programming. SBS managing director Jane Palfreyman said the broadcaster is "without question" Australia’s home of the World Cup. "The FIFA World Cup is one of the few sporting events that truly brings Australians together across all cultures, languages and communities," she said. "In 2030 audiences will once again be able to experience every match live and free on SBS."

news.title: Lionel Messi's Argentina Story: Heartbreak, Redemption And World Cup Glory
news.lede: Lionel Messi’s international career has come to an end, closing a remarkable chapter that began more than two decades ago and stretched beyond 200 appearances for Argentina. From a disastrous debut to World Cup heartbreak, near misses and, finally, the biggest prizes in the game, these were the moments that shaped Messi’s story with the national team. Here’s a look back A Blink And Miss Debut Messi first pulled on an Argentina shirt in 2005, aged just 18. His senior debut lasted barely two minutes.

news.title: Lionel Messi and Argentina: A love story that changed international football forever
news.lede: Lionel Messi and Argentina's story was never a straightforward one. It began with a choice, endured years of heartbreak and came alive with glory before finally reaching its bittersweet ending. As Messi says goodbye to the Albiceleste, football's greatest love story comes to a close.

news.title: Messi's legendary run for Argentina almost never happened after heartbreak
news.lede: Lionel Messi rose to the legendary status of Diego Maradona, but the road to glory started with heartbreak. (Getty Images: Anychance/Simon Bruty). Lionel Messi's retirement from the Argentina national side brings down the curtain on one of world football's most storied international careers. The records and achievements of Messi are stuff of legend, and his status in international sport is reserved for only the very greatest of their craft.
